Each sale can have multiple images with order, alt text, and URLs. Sellers can reorder images, update alt text for accessibility, add new images, or delete existing ones.

The operation validates the provided saleId path parameter as a UUID referencing an existing sale.

The request body accepts an array of update information objects for sale images, following the DTO schema `IShoppingMallSaleImage.IUpdate` which reflects the database fields including image URL, display order, and alternative text.

The response is a paginated summary list of the updated sale images, reflecting their new order and metadata post-update, leveraging the DTO `IPageIShoppingMallSaleImage.ISummary` which includes pagination metadata.

Authorization requires the requesting user to be the seller owning the sale or an administrator.

This endpoint supports transactional updates to maintain consistency in image ordering and linkage to the sale entity.

The service layer should validate the saleId parameter to confirm the sale exists and belongs to the authorized user.

Begin a database transaction to update the sale images atomically.

For each image update object in the request body:
- Validate the image URL is a valid URI string.
- Validate the display order is a positive integer.
- Update existing images or insert new ones as needed with the provided data.
- Support deletion of images not included in the request by comparing existing images for the sale.

Enforce the unique constraint on (shopping_mall_sale_id, display_order) to prevent duplicate display orders.

Commit the transaction after all updates succeed.

Return the paginated list of updated images for the sale, ordered by display_order.

Handle errors gracefully, returning appropriate HTTP status codes and error messages for authorization failure, validation errors, or database conflicts.

Ensure logging of changes for auditability, referencing business rules in requirement documents about product image changes being captured in snapshots.

Integrate with file storage service if image URLs require upload processing (outside the immediate scope of this API).

This operation is intended for administrators to manage product categorization hierarchy by removing a subcategory. Upon deletion, products under this subcategory become uncategorized as per system rules.

Security
- Only administrators are authorized to invoke this operation.

Database Entity
- Target entity is shopping_mall_product_subcategories table which relates to shopping_mall_product_categories.

- Both productCategoryId and productSubcategoryId must be valid existing identifiers.

- Successful operation removes the subcategory permanently from database.
- Associated products are reassigned to uncategorized.

Related Operations
- GET /admins/categories to list and preview categories and subcategories.

Service layer:
- Validate that productCategoryId and productSubcategoryId exist and belong together.
- Verify administrator authorization.
- Use transactional deletion from shopping_mall_product_subcategories.
- Reassign products in this subcategory to uncategorized state in shopping_mall_products.
- Return HTTP 204 No Content on successful deletion.

Database queries:
- DELETE FROM shopping_mall_product_subcategories WHERE id = {productSubcategoryId} AND product_category_id = {productCategoryId}.
- UPDATE shopping_mall_products SET product_subcategory_id = NULL WHERE product_subcategory_id = {productSubcategoryId}.

Error handling:
- Return 404 if identifiers are invalid or not matched.
- Return 403 if unauthorized.
- Return 500 for unexpected errors.

operations.description:
Approve a customer cancellation request for a specific order item.

This endpoint allows authorized sellers or administrators to approve a cancellation request submitted by a customer for an order item that is in a "paid" status. Upon approval, the order item's status is updated to "cancelled", the stock quantity for the associated product variant is restored, and an immutable snapshot record of the cancellation request and its approval status is created for compliance and audit purposes.

Security and Authorization:
Only users authenticated as sellers or administrators have permission to invoke this endpoint. Customers and unauthenticated users are denied access.

Entities and Relationships:
- The primary entity is `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` representing customer requests for cancellation on specific order items.
- Related `shopping_mall_order_items` are updated when cancellations are approved.
- `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots` are created to preserve immutable state of requests.

Business Logic and Validation:
- The request to approve must be on a cancellation request currently in a pending or review state.
- Approval triggers update of order item status and stock restoration.
- Partial cancellations affect only selected items without cancelling the entire order.

Related API Operations:
- POST `/cancellation-requests/{cancellationRequestId}/reject` for rejecting cancellation requests.
- GET `/cancellation-requests/{cancellationRequestId}` to view details of a cancellation request.

Expected Behavior and Error Handling:
- If the cancellation request ID does not exist, the API returns 404 Not Found.
- If the request is in an invalid state for approval, a 400 Bad Request error is returned.
- Network and server errors return standard error responses with appropriate codes.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
1. Verify the caller's authorization as seller or administrator.
2. Validate the existence of the cancellation request by `cancellationRequestId`.
3. Check that the cancellation request is in a state allowing approval (e.g., pending).
4. Update the cancellation request status to approved.
5. Update the linked order item status to "cancelled".
6. Restore stock quantities in the inventory for the cancelled items.
7. Create an immutable snapshot in `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots` recording the approval event and any notes.
8. Return the updated cancellation request entity with approval details.
9. Handle error states appropriately, returning meaningful error codes and messages.

responseBody.description: The updated cancellation request resource reflecting approval status

parameters.name: cancellationRequestId

operations.description:
This API endpoint allows an authenticated user to mark one or more notifications as read. It accepts a list of notification IDs in the request body and updates their read status, read timestamp, and is_read flag.

The notifications belong to the authenticated user, whose ownership and authorization are verified before updates.

The underlying data model is the shopping_mall_user_notifications table, which tracks notification metadata such as title, body, URLs, images, delivery and read timestamps, and read flags.

The response returns the current summaries of the updated notifications after applying the read status update.

This operation ensures only the owner user can mark their notifications as read and handles partial update scenarios robustly.

Errors include 404 for not found notifications and 403 for unauthorized access attempts.

No soft delete logic is involved in marking notifications as read.

Related operations include GET /notifications for fetching notifications and PATCH /notifications/unread for marking notifications as unread if implemented.

> This operation is essential for user notification management in the shopping mall platform, enhancing user experience by allowing them to keep track of their notification statuses.

operations.specification:
- Validate authenticated user identity and notification ownership.
- Accept request body with array of notification IDs.
- For each notification ID, verify notification exists and belongs to the user.
- Update is_read to true and set read_at timestamp.
- Return updated notification summary data.
- Handle transactions to ensure atomicity.
- Errors for missing or unauthorized notifications.
- Integration with notification delivery and logging subsystems.
- Audit trail of read status changes.
- This operation is triggered by user action in notification UI.

Approve a pending administrator request identified by the unique requestId.

This operation allows authorized administrators to approve requests from customers or sellers who want to become administrators. The approval updates the request's status field to 'approved'.

Security ensures only administrators can perform this action.

The operation affects the shopping_mall_administrator_requests table, which stores polymorphic actor requests with reason and current status tracking. Soft delete is supported and respected.

Note that this is a state-change operation, so it uses POST method with no request body.

Clients must provide the UUID of the administrator request to approve in the path parameter.

The response returns the updated administrator request entity including all metadata fields.
operations.name: approveAdministratorRequest
operations.specification:
Upon receiving the requestId in the path, validate that the request exists and is in 'pending' status. Check that the caller is authorized as an administrator.

Update the status field to 'approved' and set updated_at to current timestamp.

Return the full updated record of shopping_mall_administrator_requests identified by requestId.

Handle error responses if requestId does not exist, is already approved/rejected, or caller lacks permissions.

operations.description:
Suspend a seller account by creating a new suspension record.

This operation is used by administrators to suspend a seller. Suspending a seller hides their products, disables product creation and editing, but allows processing existing orders.

The seller is identified by the path parameter sellerId which corresponds to a valid seller account.

The request body must contain a suspensionReason explaining the cause for suspension for audit trails.

Upon success, the system creates a suspension record in shopping_mall_seller_suspensions containing the reason and suspended timestamp.

This operation requires administrator authorization.

Related operations:
- GET /admins/sellers to view sellers
- PUT /admins/sellers/{sellerId}/ban to ban/unban sellers

Error cases include validation failure if sellerId not found, or missing suspensionReason in body.

Note: This is a hard action creating a suspension record. There is no soft delete implemented here.
operations.name: suspend
operations.specification:
Service layer logic:
- Validate if sellerId exists and is active.
- Parse suspensionReason from requestBody.
- Create new record in shopping_mall_seller_suspensions with seller_id, suspension_reason, suspended_at (current timestamp), created_at, updated_at.
- Return the created suspension record in response.

Database queries:
- SELECT to validate seller existence.
- INSERT into shopping_mall_seller_suspensions.

Business rules:
- Only administrators can perform this. Authorization enforced externally.
- Multiple suspension records for same seller allowed to track history.
- Suspension disables product creation and editing but permits existing order fulfillment.

Edge cases:
- If sellerId does not exist, return error.
- If suspensionReason missing, return validation error.

Integration:
- May trigger notification to seller (outside scope here).

responseBody.description: The created suspension record confirming the seller is suspended

parameters.description: UUID of the seller to be suspended
parameters.name: sellerId

requestBody.description: Details of suspension reason

operations.description:
This operation allows an administrator to unsuspend a suspended seller account by removing or marking the suspension as lifted for the targeted seller identified by the sellerId path parameter.

Suspensions are stored in the shopping_mall_seller_suspensions table, linked to the shopping_mall_sellers table by sellerId. Unsuspending a seller restores their ability to create and edit products, and makes their products visible to customers again.

Security:
Only authorized administrators with seller management permissions should access this operation.

Database Interaction:
This operation deletes or deactivates the current suspension record for the seller and updates the seller record accordingly.

Validation:
It ensures the seller exists and is currently suspended. If not suspended, returns an appropriate error status.

Related Operations:
Admins may also suspend sellers via a corresponding suspend operation.

Error Handling:
Returns 404 if the sellerId does not exist or is not currently suspended.
Returns 403 if the caller lacks sufficient permissions.
operations.name: unsuspend
operations.specification:
The service implementation should perform the following steps:
1. Validate that the sellerId exists in the shopping_mall_sellers table.
2. Check the shopping_mall_seller_suspensions table for any active suspension linked to this sellerId.
3. If an active suspension exists, either delete the suspension record or mark it as lifted (soft-delete).
4. Update shopping_mall_sellers table to reflect the unsuspension status if applicable.
5. Return the updated suspension or seller entity to confirm unsuspension.
6. Enforce admin-level authorization checks before performing these actions.
7. Handle errors for non-existing sellerId or no active suspension with appropriate HTTP status codes.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of the unsuspension action including updated seller suspension state.

parameters.description: UUID of the seller to unsuspend (admin scope).
parameters.name: sellerId

The operation requires administrator authentication and authorization to ensure only privileged users can perform this action.

The operation targets the shopping_mall_banned_users database table where banned users' records are stored. It looks for the customer ban record using the given customerId UUID parameter.

Upon success, the ban record related to the specified customer is deleted, lifting the restriction on their account.

No request body is required since the unban operation is determined solely by the path parameter.

No response body is returned; success is indicated by HTTP status 200 or 204.

This operation belongs to the administrative functions API subset related to user account banning management.

Related operations include banning a customer via PUT /banned-users/customers/{customerId}/ban and querying banned customers via GET /banned-users/customers.

Return HTTP 204 No Content on successful unban.

operations.description:
This endpoint allows administrators to ban a seller account identified by the sellerId path parameter.

Banning a seller restricts the seller's access to logging in and disables creation or editing of products by that seller. Existing orders and order processing remain unaffected. Sellers that are banned cannot access the platform but their historical data remain preserved for audit and legal compliance.

Security considerations restrict this endpoint to administrator roles only; customers and sellers cannot perform bans.

This operation directly manipulates the banned users administrative records to enforce the ban status on the specified seller.

The request requires the sellerId path parameter representing the UUID of the target seller.

No request body is needed as all necessary information is in the path parameter.

A successful response indicates the ban was applied. Failure cases such as invalid sellerId or insufficient permissions would be handled by standard error responses.

Related operations include unbanSeller at PUT /banned-users/sellers/{sellerId}/unban and getBannedSellers at GET /banned-users/sellers.
operations.name: banSeller
operations.specification:
Validate the sellerId path parameter as a UUID and verify the seller exists.

Check the caller has administrator privileges.

Add an entry in shopping_mall_banned_users linking the seller ID, recording ban reason if applicable, and timestamps.

Update seller status if needed to mark as banned.

Ensure that the seller cannot log in or create/edit products while banned.

Return a 204 No Content response on success.

Handle errors for non-existent sellerId or authorization failures with appropriate HTTP status and error messages.

Ensure idempotent behavior - banning an already banned seller returns success without duplicate entries.

Audit logs must be recorded via another system component for tracking bans.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the seller to be banned.
parameters.name: sellerId

operations.description:
This API operation enables an administrator to unban a suspended seller by specifying the seller's unique identifier (sellerId in UUID format).

Administrators with the necessary authorization can use this endpoint to reinstate a seller's account, allowing the seller to regain access to platform functionalities such as logging in and managing their products and orders.

The path parameter `sellerId` uniquely identifies the banned seller within the system. Only authorized administrator actors have permission to perform this action.

Upon successful execution, the operation returns no content (HTTP 204). No request body is required since the seller is identified via the URL path.

This operation interacts with the database entities managing banned users and sellers, ensuring that the ban record is removed or updated accordingly. Audit logging of this action is performed for compliance and traceability.
operations.name: unbanSeller
operations.specification:

If the seller is found and currently banned, remove the ban record or update status.
Persist changes to the database.
Return a 204 No Content response upon success.
If the seller is not banned or does not exist, return appropriate error codes (404 or 400).

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of administrative audit logs with detailed information about actions performed by administrators on the platform.

This API operation is designed to support complex search filters including action types, administrator IDs, date ranges, and other audit log metadata.

Only administrators with proper authorization can access this endpoint to ensure security and confidentiality of audit data.

The underlying database entity is shopping_mall_administrative_audit_logs which captures records of administrative actions such as changes made to system settings, approvals, and other audit-related events.

The operation supports pagination with page size and cursor parameters to handle large datasets efficiently.

Clients may use this endpoint together with administrative user management APIs to correlate actions with users.

Error handling includes validation of search parameters and authorization errors.

current.description:

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:

statistics.

alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation

IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.
